title: THE AMENDMENTS
sub: 27 changes to the Constitution. The first ten, the Bill of Rights, protect you from your own government.
how: How one gets added (Article V): two-thirds of both houses of Congress propose it, and three-fourths of the states ratify it.

layer1.title: Meet the amendments
layer1.line: One card per amendment. Same words as your chart.

lines: Freedom of religion, speech and the press; the right to gather peacefully and to petition (ask the government to fix a wrong).
"A well regulated Militia, being necessary to the security of a free State, the right of the people to keep and bear Arms, shall not be infringed."
No soldiers housed in your home in peacetime without your consent.
No unreasonable searches or seizures. A warrant needs probable cause.
No trial twice for the same crime; you can't be forced to be a witness against yourself; due process; fair payment if the government takes your property.
A speedy, public trial by a fair jury. You hear the charges, face the witnesses, and get a lawyer.
A jury trial in lawsuits worth more than $20.
No excessive bail or fines. No cruel and unusual punishment.
Rights not listed here still belong to the people.
Powers not given to the national government belong to the states or the people.
Limits lawsuits in federal court against a state by people from another state or country.
Electors cast separate votes for President and Vice President.
Ends slavery.
Anyone born or naturalized here, and subject to its laws, is a citizen. No state may deny due process or the equal protection of the laws.
The right to vote can't be denied because of race or color.
Congress can tax incomes, a power the Supreme Court had said it lacked.
Voters elect their senators directly.
Bans making, selling or moving alcohol (Prohibition).
The right to vote can't be denied because of sex.
New terms start sooner: January 20 for the President, January 3 for Congress.
Ends Prohibition (repeals the 18th).
A President can be elected only twice.
Washington, D.C., gets electoral votes for President.
No poll tax in federal elections.
If the President dies, resigns or can't serve, the Vice President takes over; a vacant Vice Presidency gets filled.
The right to vote can't be denied to citizens 18 or older because of age.
A pay raise Congress votes itself waits until after the next House election.

foot: The tag beside each amendment is the principle from your card that it connects to. VOTE marks the four that say the vote can't be denied because of race, sex, a poll tax, or age.

layer2.title: Know Your Rights
layer2.line: Something happens. Tap the amendment that answers it.

items.situation: The government orders a newspaper to stop printing articles that criticize the President.
items.question: Which amendment protects the paper?
items.why: "Congress shall make no law… abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press" (1st Amendment).

items.situation: Congress passes a law making one church the official national church that everyone must pay to support.
items.question: Which amendment blocks it?
items.why: "Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion" (1st Amendment).

items.situation: Police search a man's house without a warrant and with no reason to think he did anything wrong.
items.question: Which amendment did they break?
items.why: No unreasonable searches; a warrant needs probable cause (4th Amendment).

items.situation: At her trial, a woman is told she must take the stand and answer questions that could prove her guilty.
items.question: Which amendment says she doesn't have to?
items.why: No one can be "compelled in any criminal case to be a witness against himself" (5th Amendment).

items.situation: A jury finds a man not guilty of a robbery. The prosecutor wants to try him again for the same robbery.
items.question: Which amendment stops a second trial?
items.why: No one can be tried twice for the same crime. That's called double jeopardy (5th Amendment).

items.situation: A city wants to build a highway through a family's land and take it without paying.
items.question: Which amendment says the family gets paid?
items.why: Private property can't be taken for public use "without just compensation" (5th Amendment).

items.situation: A man waits in jail for three years with no trial, and nobody gives him a lawyer.
items.question: Which amendment did the government break?
items.why: The accused gets "a speedy and public trial" and a lawyer (6th Amendment).

items.situation: A judge fines a driver $10 million for a parking ticket.
items.question: Which amendment says that's too much?
items.why: "Excessive bail shall not be required, nor excessive fines imposed" (8th Amendment).

items.situation: In peacetime, the army orders a family to let soldiers live in their house.
items.question: Which amendment lets the family say no?
items.why: No soldier can be housed in a home in peacetime "without the consent of the Owner" (3rd Amendment).

items.situation: Your state, not Congress, decides how many credits you need to graduate from high school.
items.question: Which amendment leaves that power with the states?
items.why: Powers not given to the national government are "reserved to the States respectively, or to the people" (10th Amendment).

layer2.done: You know your rights. When one shows up in a document or a headline, name it.
